about.what: Measured outcomes of `grasppanda compose` + `grasppanda probe` for the grid of grasppanda.combine.grid. No number here is an accuracy; see docs/advanced_guides/measured_combinations.md.

verdicts.runs: On real frames: the detector was built, every requested training iteration ran with finite losses and at least one real seed, every top-level part of the model that holds trainable parameters received a gradient in at least one iteration, the weights stayed finite, and prediction returned one valid grasp group for every probed frame, at least one of them with a grasp.
verdicts.runs-empty: As `runs`, except that no probed frame has a grasp: prediction returned one valid grasp group for every probed frame and every group is empty. Every stage ran; a model trained for a few iterations often keeps no seed. A run that is also unstable is `runs-unstable`.
verdicts.runs-unstable: On real frames: the detector was built, trained and predicted, but a loss or a weight became non-finite (a non-finite loss ends the training there), or an iteration had no real seed (no scene point passed the proposal, so only the proposal was trained), or no iteration supervised a seed, or a top-level part with trainable parameters received no gradient in any iteration, or fewer iterations ran or fewer frames were predicted than were asked for.
verdicts.fails: An exception was raised after the config check had passed. The report names the phase (build, data, optimizer, loss, backward, step, hook, predict), the component it came from and the message.
verdicts.refused: The config check refused the config (the same check as `grasppanda print-config --check --for train`). Nothing was built; the report carries the messages.
verdicts.wired: No real frame was read. On a synthetic table-top scene with random labels the detector was built, back-propagated a loss through every stage and predicted. This shows that the stages connect; it says nothing about real data.

fields.group: reference, encoder, stage, stage-set, family, family-slot, post, loss, recipe or cross (grasppanda.combine.grid)
fields.method: the method whose shipped config the cell starts from
fields.sets: the slot=choice pairs of the compose request; absent for a config as shipped
fields.slot, component, variant: for encoder and stage cells: the replaced slot, the component type put there, and its preset (or the type again, for constructor defaults)
fields.config_hash: first 16 hex digits of the hash of the composed config; null when the config check refused it
fields.compose: the command that wrote the config; absent for a config as shipped
fields.probe: the command that probed it, to be run after `compose` in the same directory. It repeats the experiment, not its numbers: see about.one_run
fields.schedule, rate: how the probe set the learning rate (about.schedules): `constant`, the recipe's peak rate at every step, or `recipe`, the recipe's schedule run over the probe's epochs (always for a cell whose request sets the schedule); `rate` is the rate every step used under `constant`, in the first parameter group of the first optimizer. A record without `schedule` was probed before the probe had the option, with the recipe's schedule
fields.probed_as: the cell whose probe this cell shares: both composed to the same config (the same hash), which was probed once. The numbers are in that cell
fields.adapter: the encoder adapter compose inserted, when it did
fields.fitted: options compose set to fit the method, beyond copying a preset
fields.refusal: the messages of the contract rules and of the config check, whole
fields.refusal_kinds: parallel to `refusal`, the kind of each message (about.refusal_kinds: structural, not-implemented, fixed-by-compose, not-a-combination, policy); absent in a record composed before compose reported kinds
fields.repeat: for a cell whose probe was runs-unstable: the same probe run once more (same command, seed and schedule), with the fields of a probe from `verdict` to `run`. A class counts a run as unstable only when the repeat was unstable too
fields.failure: phase, component, exception and message of a failure after the check passed
fields.parameters, iterations, batch_size, fram: what the probe built, trained on and predicted
fields.losses: every loss term at the first and the last iteration, four significant digits
fields.real_seeds, supervised_seeds: minimum and mean over the iterations of the fraction of seed slots with a real seed and of seeds that took part in the grasp losses, and the number of iterations at zero
fields.judge: 2 for a record judged by judge 2, which holds the fields from `trend` to `lr_factor`; absent for a record of the first judge, which holds none of them (about.judges)
fields.trend: per loss term and for the total `loss`, over the iterations in which the term was active (reported, finite and not exactly 0.0): [first, last_quarter, fall], its value at the first of them, the mean of the last ceil(active / 4) of them, and (first - last_quarter) / |first|, positive when the term fell (0.7: by 70 %), to four significant digits and three decimals; three nulls when the term was never active
fields.active: per loss term active in fewer iterations than ran: the number it was active in
fields.flags: per loss term with a flag: the flags that hold. `flat`: the term was active in at least two iterations, and the mean of its last quarter differs from its first active value by less than 5 % of that value; `rising`: the term was active in at least two iterations, and the mean of the last half of its active iterations exceeds the mean of the first half by more than 10 % of the first half's mean (with an odd count the middle iteration is in neither half); `zero_at_end`: the term is exactly 0.0, or not reported, at the last completed iteration; `constant`: the term was reported in at least two iterations with the very same value in every one of them, zeros included
fields.no_gradient: the units of the model whose gradient never had an L2 norm above 1e-8 in an iteration, over its trainable parameters. A unit is a registered sub-module at depth 2 (`backbone.encoder`, `head.score_net`) or a parameter a top-level part holds itself (`head.bias`); when no unit of a top-level part was reached, the part is listed instead of its units (`backbone`: a dead part). Gradients are read before every optimizer step, unscaled under mixed precision. In a record of the first judge (only when its probe had the check): the top-level parts without a non-zero gradient
fields.unchanged: the top-level parts whose trainable parameters did not change: the L2 norm of the difference between before the first optimizer step and after the last one is at most 1e-6 times the larger of 1 and the L2 norm before
fields.checked: [units, parts] with trainable parameters, over which `no_gradient` and `unchanged` were checked
fields.score_quantiles: per predicted frame, the smallest, the median and the largest score of its predicted grasps, to 4 significant digits; null for a frame without a grasp. Scores are those the detector returns (their meaning is its `score_kind`)
fields.learning_rate, lr_factor: the learning rate of the first parameter group of the first optimizer at the first and at the last optimizer step, as those steps used it; the last of these divided by the first: the decay the schedule applied within the probe. A schedule that steps per epoch decays with the probe's epochs, which follow from the batch size and the number of frames (GSNet's 0.95 per epoch: 0.95^9 after 20 iterations of 2 per epoch); 1 under the schedule `constant`; null when the first is 0
fields.losses_per_iteration: not in this file: the side file measured_combinations/losses_per_iteration.json holds, for every cell of judge 2 with a probe of its own, every loss term and the total `loss` at every completed iteration, to 4 significant digits; null where the detector did not report the term
fields.shared_machine: seconds per iteration, peak GPU memory (MiB) and wall time of the probe (s): numbers that depend on the load of the machine
fields.postprocessing: for post cells: the steps of the variant `post`, and per predicted frame the number of grasps predicted and left after every step. The grasps are those of a detector trained for the iterations of the probe
fields.notes: what the probe changed or noticed, in its own words: for example a batch smaller than the recipe's because the split has fewer frames
fields.run: the run that measured the cell (about.runs): date, commit and environment. A record is bound to that commit: it is replaced when its config changes, not when the code of a component does

about.one_run: A cell is one run, and training on a GPU is not repeatable here. The config hash and the parameter count repeat exactly and the losses of the first iteration to the digits given; later losses, `real_seeds`, `supervised_seeds`, `grasps_per_frame` and, for a combination near the edge, the split between `runs` and `runs-unstable` are those of the recorded run and differ in the next one.
about.scale_statistic: Configs that read the width histogram of Scale-Balanced-Grasp were probed with the reference's own file (`scale_statistic.source: legacy_import`, the SHA-256 in the probe command): the native histogram is a statistic of a whole training split, and a probe reads eight frames.
about.shared_machine: `shared_machine` holds seconds per iteration, peak GPU memory and wall time. They were measured while other jobs used the same GPU and CPUs, with as many probes at a time as the run says: an order of magnitude, not a benchmark.
about.judges: A record with `judge: 2` was judged by judge 2 (grasppanda.combine.probe, from 2026-10-15): `runs-empty` is a verdict, a dead top-level part makes a run `runs-unstable`, and the record holds the trend and flags of every loss term, the units without a gradient, the unchanged parts, the score quantiles and the learning-rate decay; the loss of every iteration is in the side file. A record without `judge` was judged by the first judge: it had no `runs-empty` (a run that predicted no grasp on any frame is `runs`), it holds none of those fields, and it was checked for dead top-level parts only if its probe had that check (then `no_gradient` is in the record).

schedules.recipe: the config's own scheduler, run over the probe. The probe sets `train.epochs` to ceil(iterations / iterations per epoch), so a schedule that steps per epoch is compressed into those few epochs (GSNet's 0.95 per epoch ends at 0.95^9 = 0.63 after 20 iterations of 2 per epoch, EconomicGrasp's cosine at 2.4 % of its start) and one that steps per iteration runs its first steps only (FineGrasp's warm-up of 800 iterations keeps a probe of 20 at no more than 2.5 % of its rate)
schedules.constant: no scheduler: every parameter group of every optimizer trains at the recipe's peak rate for the whole probe. The peak is the rate the optimizer gives the group (the configured `lr`, with the multipliers of ParamGroups), except for a schedule that sets a peak of its own: `max_lr` of OneCycleLR and CyclicLR, the larger factor of LinearLR. Every other schedule of the toolbox starts at that rate or reaches it at the end of its warm-up. When the probe's batches hold fewer frames than the recipe's, the peak is scaled by their ratio (the linear scaling rule: FineGrasp's 0.008 for 32 frames trains at 0.002 on batches of 8). A batch-norm momentum that the recipe decays per epoch (BNMomentumHook: GraspNet-baseline, Scale-Balanced-Grasp, HGGD) is held at its first epoch's value likewise (`hooks.<i>.decay=1`): decayed over epochs of a few iterations it can reach its floor of 0.001 within the probe (Scale-Balanced-Grasp's at iteration 73), and the running statistics, which prediction normalises with, then stop following the weights; training itself does not read them. The optimizer (its weight decay and its momentum as configured), clipping, accumulation and every other hook are the recipe's

presets_without_a_cell.post/target-mask: reads observation.masks, which no shipped dataset fills
presets_without_a_cell.loss/distribution-focal: fits `bins` terms only, which no shipped method has; probed as the width loss of the head preset `decoupled-grid-bins` (stage cells)
